text: We must give them resources and support, across life stages.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This next phase will require us to build a culture that is more open to failure, if you learn from it.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We need to teach our kids and their parents that it is not just the bankers, doctors, lawyers, chief executive officers, Ministers with straight-"A"s and a fast-track career that deserve to be admired and emulated, but the business owner who overcame failures.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We need to teach our kids that success is not a function of Tik Tok views and likes, but of hard work and discipline, struggle and sacrifice.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: While we build new growth areas for Singaporeans, the skills required to jumpstart and grow these fields are currently in short supply globally, and countries are racing to build the same skills.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The competition for highly skilled workers is shifting into the geopolitical sphere, leveraging tools like immigration policy.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Singapore has always been forward-looking in this area, attracting top science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) talents, reaching out to our diaspora, developing Global Innovation Alliances.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Back in the mid-2000s, as the Economic Development Board's (EDB's) Boston Center Director, my husband supported Mr Philip Yeo, who was then building up the biomedical sciences sector in his meetings with some of the biggest names in life sciences.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: They came to set up labs here, grooming Singapore talents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Now, we need highly skilled talents in AI, quantum, green energy, nuclear fusion, and people with experience commercialising and scaling these innovations in these areas.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We should look at what more we can do to win the geopolitical competition for talent, such as better headhunting with network analysis, allocating global talent funds, tapping on remote talent and building global talent ecosystems.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: A credible strategy to attract the best and brightest globally requires solid political support, and that starts with improving the conditions for all citizens to thrive.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In tandem with skilling and job creation, we have done a lot to strengthen our social safety nets, make Singapore more family friendly, and promote physical and mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In my Budget 2023 speech, I advocated for more support for Singaporeans who had lost their jobs, ex-offenders and those struggling with debt, after seeing some of my Woodlands residents in these situations.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Each of these groups is now receiving more support and will receive more support under Budget 2025.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I will continue to push for vulnerable groups, and for policy implementation to go apace, not get overtaken by cost increases or other events that reduce the real value of the support.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In the Committee of Supply (COS) debate, I will speak on the need to ensure that policies land in a human-centred way on the ground, with those at the frontline empowered to deliver support consistent with the policy intent, and to make the calls for deviations for deserving cases.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: On families, I have spoken for more paternity leave, flexible work arrangements and childcare leave for those with more children.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In the COS debate, I will ask for more help for parents to cope with raising children, so they can enjoy the experience for the blessing that it is.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And let us give more support to those who are trying so hard to have children.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Together with Dr Wan Rizal and others, we tabled the Mental Health Motion.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I shared the stories of my Woodlands residents, including one who succumbed to suicide.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I am grateful for their support and input.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In the COS debate, I will push for elevating mental health, closing the gaps between mental health and physical health support.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Just as self-determination is a foundational value for Singapore, self-determination must remain a core value for Singaporeans, who must, in turn, be empowered and supported when they face job losses, health crises and personal setbacks.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Collective responsibility breeds unity which breeds collective responsibility, a virtuous cycle.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Volunteers from all over Singapore, including Sengkang, help us run the store.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I am reminded of the words of former Senior Minister, President Tharman, here: "No one has a monopoly over compassion." No one, no party, has a monopoly over trying our best, overcoming hurdles, to help our residents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We all have to use our ingenuity, creativity and networks to make it a collective responsibility in our communities.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In this way, we make our people more resilient in a shifting geopolitical landscape.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But we must also recognise our geopolitical influence.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Jaafar, you might want to round up.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will not be able to respond to all of them today.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I assure you that we have heard every suggestion and we will study them carefully.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The detailed issues relating to specific programmes and schemes will be addressed later at the COS debate.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The questions raised by Members during this debate revolve around three main issues.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, how are we supporting businesses and workers to navigate our new economic reality?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, how are we helping Singaporeans to cope with the strains and stresses of life?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And third, are we overly conservative in our fiscal projections and plans?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, how do we navigate a very uncertain global environment so that we can continue to create good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Quite a number of Members spoke about this, including Ms Foo Mee Har, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Darryl David, Mr Edward Chia and Ms Mariam Jaafar just now.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can see it unfolding in real-time before our eyes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The multilateral trading system has been weakened by growing protectionist sentiments and unilateral measures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Countries are focusing more on their defence and security interests.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it has become more about zero-sum competition rather than win-win cooperation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these will disadvantage small and open economies like Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The major powers say they do not want to fight; they do not want conflict, but they are preparing for conflict.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of them realise that there is a need for a strong industrial base to sustain any war effort.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, the Western countries feel that they are at a disadvantage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Twenty years ago, China accounted for just 9% of global manufacturing output.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It accounts for one-third of global manufacturing output.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is more than the next three countries, the US, Germany and Japan, put together.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, naturally, there is a huge attempt to rebuild manufacturing in America and Europe, and that is why competition for investments will only intensify.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are taking steps to strengthen our infrastructure, enhance our enterprise ecosystem, as well as our innovation and technology engines.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These moves will translate eventually and ultimately to better jobs and better opportunities for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have to brace ourselves for increased scrutiny of high-tech activities done out of Singapore, something which we discussed in Parliament last week and which several Members also highlighted.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We welcome and harness technology from different countries.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the key countries, the key sources of technology, are now concerned about technology leakage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They want to keep their proprietary technologies controlled tightly within a safe ecosystem.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be clear, we do not enforce the unilateral export controls imposed by any single country.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will make efforts to address these concerns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will lean forward and provide assistance where appropriate in accordance with our laws.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members may have read in the media today some actions we have taken.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We made these proactive moves because we want to ensure Singapore remains a reliable and trusted partner in global trade and commerce.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In today's fragmented world, we must work even harder to stay open as a hub, where businesses from all over the world can operate with assurance and confidence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we navigate these external challenges, we also must continue to press on with productivity improvements in our own economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of this is driven by the outward-oriented sectors of our economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we can still do better to improve productivity for our domestic-oriented sectors.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know many SMEs are concerned about the high costs of doing business.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, including Senior Minister of State Desmond Tan, Mr Mark Lee and Mr Lim Biow Chuan, reflected these concerns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are economic realities we cannot avoid.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our land cost reflects its scarcity in our small island nation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As long as Singapore does well and there is strong demand for land, there will be upward pressure on land prices.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our energy costs are affected by global price levels.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We import our energy and we have limited renewable energy options.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our labour cost reflects the wages of Singaporean workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But wage increases have to be matched by productivity gains.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim highlighted that wage increases in recent years have lagged productivity growth and there is scope for wages to go up further.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we should be looking at the data over a longer timeframe.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to push for this – to push for higher productivity as well as higher wages.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we opted for the Progressive Wage Model, which ensures continued skills upgrading for workers as they move up the wage ladder.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we are increasing co-funding levels for the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme to help companies co-pay the wage increases for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also supporting companies on the regulatory front.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He will give an update on this work at the Ministry of Trade and Industry's (MTI's) COS debate.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our more important effort is really to help companies consolidate, restructure and transform.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is something the Government can encourage, facilitate and nudge.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in the end, the business owners themselves, the companies themselves, must be prepared to make the change.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some retailers are concerned about the impact of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with e-commerce, competition is already happening and it is happening and taking place from all over the world.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, Singapore consumers, all of us, can already purchase many items from abroad and have them shipped to our doorsteps at cheaper prices than the local retail price.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, retailers have to adapt and re-think their business models.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of baking supplies company Phoon Huat.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It started out in 1947 as a single shop in Middle Road.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with continuous transformation, it has expanded its operations significantly.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It now has its own production facility, a distribution centre and 20 retail stores in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And with support from Enterprise Singapore, it has built a thriving e-commerce platform, which enables it to export to more than 20 countries.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has also adapted to changing consumer preferences, for example, by launching its own gourmet brand and refreshing its brick-and-mortar stores to provide experiential spaces for baking demonstrations and classes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is how constant innovation and transformation can allow businesses to stay competitive and relevant.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not easy to make such transformations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for firms that are willing to do so, the Government will provide our full support.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked about the kind of support that is available.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have many schemes to help our SMEs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These new initiatives arose out of our engagements with the trade associations and chambers (TACs) and the Singapore Business Federation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We continue to welcome their feedback and their important work in getting their members to transform their businesses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, aside from the new initiatives, there are many existing initiatives for SMEs that remain part of our overall enterprise support efforts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For firms that fully utilise the support schemes, the total amount of help that they can get is, in fact, considerable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the past, the utilisation of many of our enterprise schemes has tended to be lower than what we had projected or hoped for.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have been discussing with the TACs to find out why, so that we can raise awareness amongst the SMEs and also do what we can to make the schemes more accessible.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides uplifting the overall SME sector, we are also developing a pipeline of promising enterprises, some of which will eventually grow to become global companies of the future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The multinational enterprises (MNEs) we attract to Singapore support this enterprise development strategy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because the smaller firms can partner with the MNEs and eventually expand to new markets abroad.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Neil Parekh highlighted, such partnerships are beneficial and we will continue to create more opportunities for collaboration.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some enterprises are started by global entrepreneurs or founders from abroad who are keen to use Singapore as a launchpad and we welcome more of them to come here and to launch their next big idea here.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are also homegrown companies emerging from our research and development (R&D) ecosystem, which Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat mentioned yesterday.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And more young Singaporeans are now prepared to take the plunge into entrepreneurship.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, on the whole, if you look at our enterprise ecosystem today compared to 15 years ago, I would say things have improved considerably.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is still much more that needs to be done and we will press on with our efforts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With constant industry transformation, we can expect more churn in workplaces – existing jobs will be redesigned and new jobs will be created.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Understandably, all these will contribute to anxiety and concerns amongst Singaporeans about jobs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, like Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Faisal Manap spoke about this; and Ms Denise Phua and Ms Jessica Tan also highlighted the disruptions that could be posed by rapid technological advances.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because we can see this happening in so many other countries, where foreigners are blamed and the public discourse ends up spiralling into very negative, toxic and xenophobic directions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is not what we stand for in Singapore and we must never allow that to happen here.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We welcome them to work here, but we do this in a controlled manner and ensure they complement Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we have continued to finetune, over time, our system of controls.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have introduced the Complementary Assessment (COMPASS) framework for Employment Passes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have introduced new measures, like the Workplace Fairness Act, to protect Singaporeans against workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This approach has contributed to positive outcomes, including low overall unemployment rates, good employment outcomes and rising real incomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are not resting on our laurels.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will do more to better support Singaporeans, young and old, to better equip everyone for the changes in our economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is exactly why we are taking decisive steps to strengthen SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been 10 years since we started, as some Members highlighted.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we are making further moves, including to nurture more promising Singaporean corporate leaders and we will do more.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members also spoke about this, including Miss Cheryl Chan about a talent development strategy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to develop Singaporean talent and we want to see more Singaporeans take on leadership positions in the corporate sector.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also supporting in this Budget senior worker employment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is something close to the heart of many labour Members of Parliament (MPs) and many of them spoke about this passionately – Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are convening the Tripartite Workgroup to dive deeper.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There will be many issues to work through and I look forward to making progress with all of them with our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, while we have made progress on SkillsFuture, we know that there is still much more to be done.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because you can compare our adult education and training system with all the investments and established infrastructure we have in the formal schooling years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is still so much to do to fully build up our SkillsFuture system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you look around the world, in countries everywhere, generally, governments have invested more in pre-employment training than in adult education and training.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But compared to other countries, in fact, Singapore is already at the forefront in many respects.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there are no ready models for us to look to.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to experiment, innovate and find our own way forward.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are fully committed to this endeavour and I expect to put in additional resources in the coming years to further strengthen SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will create even more opportunities and better jobs for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This leads to the second issue, which is, how is the Government providing enough support to help Singaporeans cope with other stressors and strains in life?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Pritam Singh, the Leader of the Opposition and Mr Leong Mun Wai said Goods and Services Tax (GST) increase has made it worse by adding to inflation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, Mr Singh said that the GST increase "turbocharged" inflation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a small and open economy, our inflation was driven primarily by global factors – wars, supply chain disruptions, and rising energy costs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat noted, even before the GST increase, prices were already going up globally and in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And here in Singapore, the central bank, MAS, had assessed that the effect of the GST increase on inflation would be "transitory".

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look, I know elections are approaching, but this Chamber is not an election rally.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us not get carried away by the hyperbole, but have a debate based on facts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fact is inflation has eased, both globally and in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But people are still concerned about cost pressures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is felt across many other advanced economies, where the headline economic indicators are positive, but sentiments are poor.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the US, they even coined a name for it.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is a reason for the negative vibes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just about feelings and sentiment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is because price levels remain high even though inflation has eased and these create real pressures, and it takes time for people to adjust to these new price realities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are continuing to provide temporary help measures through the CDC Vouchers and other measures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And for the one-off SG60 surplus sharing package, we decided that a key plank would also be in the form of vouchers, so that they can also provide some relief on the cost front.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I said in my Budget Statement, we will continue to provide cost of living support for as long as needed and within our means.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Workers' Party (WP) and the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) appear to be unhappy and displeased that the Government is providing vouchers to help Singaporeans with the cost of living.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They suggest that the Government is relying solely on vouchers to help with the cost of living.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, they only make up a small part of our overall Budget.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A much larger part of our spending is in structural programmes, especially to equip and empower Singaporeans through education, skills training, skills upgrading, job training and the significant moves we are making on SkillsFuture which I highlighted just now.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these will ensure Singaporeans do not just receive help but are able to stand on their own feet and seize better opportunities for themselves and thrive in a rapidly changing world.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we have repeatedly emphasised, the more durable and sustainable way to tackle cost of living is to ensure that Singaporeans enjoy higher real incomes, and that must be supported by a strong economy and productivity gains.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That remains the key thrust of our approach.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And objectively speaking, we have done relatively well.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporean households, across different income levels, have experienced sustained real income growth over the past decade.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And what we have achieved has outperformed many other advanced economies, as we can see from this chart.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I show these statistics not to blow our own trumpet, but so we know what the facts are and how we compare with other economies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I fully recognise that even with a strong and growing economy, the day-to-day lived realities for Singaporeans may be different.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Life in a compact city like Singapore, with no hinterland, can be competitive and it can be stressful – something which Members on both sides of the House were quick to bring up in their speeches over the last two days.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is exactly why as part of Forward SG, we have been taking steps to strengthen our social support system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to provide greater assurance to Singaporeans across every life stage on their basic needs, like education, retirement, healthcare and housing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to provide more support for the disadvantaged and vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to ensure that no one is left to fend for themselves in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if anyone faces setbacks, we have a system in place to help them recover and bounce back stronger.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are desired outcomes which I am sure we can all agree to.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The question is how do we achieve them?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Hazel Poa said we need to put more emphasis on social rather than economic considerations and that we are overly reliant on the price mechanism, citing land as an example.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But pricing all resources properly is not about giving more weight to economic over social considerations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is simply about getting our policies right and doing things the right way.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we do not price properly, then we are giving a hidden subsidy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If it is not paid by consumers, it is paid by taxpayers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If it is not paid today, it will have to be paid tomorrow.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because at the end of the day, there is no free lunch.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, our approach must be to get the price right, then, we decide how much to subsidise.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) has to pay the market price for the land when it develops a new flat.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But when it prices the new flat for sale, it does not recover fully the cost of the flat.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, it prices it on the basis of affordability, as we have said time and again.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will give you a concrete example: a 4-room Build-To-Order (BTO) flat in Sengkang.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was in the October 2024 BTO exercise.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, resale prices have gone up nearly $200,000.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What about the sale price by HBD for the new flat?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The BTO price has not gone up by that much.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, resale prices have gone up a lot.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: BTO, yes, but not as much and in line with median incomes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The difference is a subsidy that is borne by the Government.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That, together with the higher cost of construction, is one of the key reasons why HDB's deficit has increased sharply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government's funding to HDB to cover its deficit has correspondingly increased over the years to cover the deficit.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of you may ask and this is the right question to ask: is this sustainable?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will not be sustainable if overall property prices keep rising faster than incomes and the financing gap keeps growing year after year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this will not happen, because we keep a close watch over the property market and we ensure it does not happen.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have introduced cooling measures where necessary, by increasing the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) for multiple property and foreigner purchases and we have significantly increased BTO supply as well as Government Land Sales to make up for the disruption that occurred during COVID-19.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures have helped and will eventually stabilise the market.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More specifically, when you look at the HDB market, in the short term, resale prices can be up, they can be down.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In localised popular areas, they will generally be higher than the less-popular areas.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we introduced a new classification system with the Plus and Prime flats.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But overall, in the longer term, we are confident that HDB prices will remain affordable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can and we will build enough housing for every Singaporean household.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, we have focused on ensuring that the new flats are available for first-timers, especially young married couples and parents with young children.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The application rate for first-timer families across all flat types has stabilised.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With a sustained and robust supply of new flats and as the overall market stabilises, we will have scope to consider how to adjust our policies to meet the needs of other groups, including second-timers and singles.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There have also been calls for us, for the Government, to make bolder moves on social policies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many examples of social support arrangements that started with the best of intentions, but only ended up with more problems.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, some promise sizeable pension payments funded by younger generations, but now have problems paying for them.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others offer free universal healthcare, but now face rising costs and an overburdened healthcare system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are prepared to spend more, where necessary.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is equally if not more important to get the policies right and to ensure the overall system is fiscally sound and sustainable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On that basis, we have been taking steps to progressively strengthen the key pillars of our social system and our social compact.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started in Singapore with the basics: universal access to primary school for education, Central Provident Fund (CPF) for retirement, Government subsidies and the 3Ms – MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund – for healthcare and HDB for housing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have got Workfare Income Supplement for lower-wage workers, Silver Support for the more vulnerable seniors and SkillsFuture to support all our workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our CPF system will be 70 years old this year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a time where many pension systems are struggling with sustainability, we continue to provide assurance for Singaporeans' retirement adequacy in a sustainable manner.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At its core, the CPF enables Singaporeans to save for their own retirement, with support from their employers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we do not just leave this to individuals alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Families are encouraged to help their loved ones save more and we provide avenues for them to do so, with matching grants from the Government.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government provides risk-free interest rates, with extra interest for lower balances to boost savings.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We support lower-wage workers to earn more and save more through Workfare and progressive wages.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And for seniors who had lower incomes during their working years and so less in retirement, we have Silver Support to cover them.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These improvements have been made to CPF over the years, and more recently, when we looked at the data, we saw the need to do more for two groups.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members of Parliament, in particular, Mr Louis Chua and Mr Saktiandi Supaat, spoke at length about retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have listened to them carefully and we will consider all your views and suggestions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the recommendations of the CPF Advisory Panel, many have, in fact, already been taken up.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are now various low-cost funds included under the CPF Investment Scheme, which members can choose to invest in.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The question is whether there is scope for a low-cost life cycle fund done in a more comprehensive and structured way, beyond just leaving CPF members to choose for themselves.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They can choose but whether there is scope to do it in a more structured way.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we were to do that, that fund must be able to earn better returns than the prevailing Special Account rate, not the Ordinary Account rate.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is 4% on a risk-free basis and up to 6% based on the extra interest.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Actually, that is not easy to beat on a consistent basis.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sure, you can opt to take more risks for higher returns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Louis Chua mentioned an 80:20 portfolio promising above 7% returns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But that is, I think he qualified, potential returns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you are lucky, you may get 7% or more.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What happens if you are not so lucky?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What happens if you retire at a time of market downturn?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these are issues we will have to consider carefully.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will certainly continue to review, finetune and improve the CPF system to better meet the needs of our seniors and to prepare for a future with increased longevity and life expectancy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This same approach applies to other areas too, which many Members spoke about.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, many MPs, Mr Vikram Nair, Assoc Prof Razwana Begum, Ms Hany Soh, Mr Alex Yam, Ms Nadia Samdin, Mr Louis Ng, Ms Carrie Tan, amongst others, spoke about more support for families.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And support not just in terms of financial support, but leave arrangements was a popular refrain in the speeches.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to look at all of these suggestions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others like Ms Denise Phua, Mr Don Wee, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Sharael Taha have highlighted the need for more inclusive hiring practices and employment support for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must do more for people with disabilities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will want to do more for them.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members, such as Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Dennis Tan, also spoke about the need to help our seniors age well and ensure they are not left behind in their silver years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have made significant moves over the past one to two years to support these groups, including in this Budget.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But our attitude is we are never satisfied with the status quo and we will continue to review and study how we can make things better.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise on the subject of caregivers, which many Members spoke about too, including Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Sharael Taha, Ms Ng Ling Ling, Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some have sole caregivers while others will share the responsibility over several family members.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise the crucial role that caregivers play and the sacrifices they make, such as leaving employment to care for family arrangements or forgoing their careers in order to spend more time to take care of their family members.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to provide support for those who have to take up this role as it is not easy for them.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is difficult to put a monetary value on caregiving.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Furthermore, there is no one-size-fits-all approach to support caregivers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, our approach has been to provide support for the family as a whole.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this is not the end of our moves.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we will study more to see how we can further strengthen our support for caregivers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Dennis Tan, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Xie Yao Quan had suggestions on means testing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is something we grapple with all the time because there is no perfect means testing criteria.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even on incomes, we can decide on per capita household income, family income, but we do not have the data, lifelong earnings income, a whole range of criteria to use.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we know that, increasingly, it is not just about income as a means test but also wealth.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members of Parliament spoke about wealth inequality.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, you have to look at wealth measures and how do you look at that?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have Annual Value (AV) as a proxy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these are issues we will continue to finetune in terms of the means testing criteria.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Jean See, Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Gan Thiam Poh highlighted other groups that may need more support, like freelance and agency workers as well as working mothers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas earlier championed for the arts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han reminded us to ensure our arts and sports scene remains inclusive.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Miss Rachel Ong advocated for mental health issues.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are some of the key points that Members have raised.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We keep an open mind and we study all your suggestions carefully.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond ideas shared in this House, we continue to engage widely and hear views from all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do so through various participatory platforms – something which Ms He Ting Ru talked about, like citizen panels, youth panels and Alliances for Action (AfAs).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They take a lot of time, but we find them useful and we will plan to do more.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may not be able to do implement every idea, there will be differences of views.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if we cannot implement, for whatever reason, we will explain why.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our commitment, the Government's commitment, is that we will do whatever is necessary to ensure that every Singaporean feels supported at every life stage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the numbers, what we spend on, reflects this commitment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are not just saying we will do.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have done so in concrete terms and we expect social spending to continue to grow in the coming years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is partly driven by our ageing population and rising healthcare costs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also because of our efforts under Forward SG to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have fleshed out many programmes in this Budget and the previous one.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as I said, there will be more to come, as this is a multi-year effort.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, a strong social support system should not be reliant on the Government alone – even though the Government will do more, but it cannot be reliant on the Government alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do more but our actions must also be complemented by individual and community responsibility.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we very are fortunate to have charities and social service agencies doing excellent work on the ground.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will continue to work with all of them as partners to uplift our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should also add that many of the issues we are dealing with requires changes, not just in policies, but also in our attitudes and mindsets.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will spend more on healthcare, but Singaporeans also have to do their part to stay active and maintain a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has and will continue to invest in SkillsFuture, but Singaporeans must want to improve their skills, and businesses must give their workers the time and space to go for training.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why Forward SG is about strengthening our social compact.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about our shared responsibility – how we support one another, care for those in need and lift each other up.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we build a more inclusive, and a stronger and more united Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the treatment of the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) and how it contributed to the surplus.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under SINGA, we borrow for major and long-term infrastructure projects.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The spending for such projects is capitalised, which allows us to spread the expenses across the useful life of the asset.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This, as we have explained, is more equitable as the asset will benefit both current and future generations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This accounting treatment has been in place since FY2021.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, including Mr Singh, the Leader of the Opposition, Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Leong Mun Wai, questioned the need to increase the GST, given our strong fiscal position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should remind Members that we are in this strong, fiscal position precisely because the Government took the necessary steps early in this term to raise revenues.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if we were to rewind the clock and consider our situation, imagine what our situation was at the beginning of this decade?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We were in the thick of battle, fighting COVID-19.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know it feels like a bad dream and a distant memory to all of us, but those were truly tough times.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We sought the President's approval five times to draw from Past Reserves.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had no way of knowing when the pandemic would end, how the virus would mutate, how many more new waves of infection we would face, how many more restrictions we have to impose and how much deeper a fiscal hole we would end up with.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we already knew for sure that spending needs would rise over the horizon.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Healthcare spending was rising, especially with our rapidly ageing population.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We looked at different ways to raise revenues, including through property and income taxes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But these moves were still not enough to cover the expected increase in expenditure, which was sure to happen.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, what should we do then to plug the funding gap?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we had to consider the GST increase.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is never easy to raise taxes and certainly not a tax like the GST.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But governance is about making responsible choices, not just popular ones.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must ask ourselves: do we want short-term populism or long-term stability?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Do we want to kick the can down the road or take the hard but necessary decisions?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, once there were signs that the economy had stabilised, we decided to proceed with the GST increase.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also rolled out a comprehensive Assurance Package, which effectively delayed the GST increase for the vast majority of Singaporean households.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Essentially, once we decided to move, the GST rates were locked in.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with the Assurance Package, we could be more responsive to changing circumstances and we could push back effectively the impact of the GST increase.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had multiple rounds of enhancements to the Assurance Package to tackle cost of living concerns and to ensure that the majority of households will not feel the impact of the additional GST for at least five years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we also have a permanent GST Voucher scheme, which we also enhanced.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this ensures that the GST and the GST Voucher Scheme, combined together, will support the lower-income groups and will protect them, not just over the next five or 10 years, but on a permanent and ongoing basis.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, with that in place, together with the other revenue moves we made, we are in a better position now.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And now, the additional GST revenues have started to come in.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the revenues are mostly from those who are better-off, foreigners as well as tourists.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it will give us the resources we need to improve our healthcare infrastructure and take better care of our seniors.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What would have happened if we chose to avoid the GST increase because it is unpopular?

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The projected balance in FY2025 would also have been a deficit.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that would have meant less funding for essential services, less support for our seniors and fewer resources to invest in our future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Basically, Singapore and Singaporeans would have ended up in a much weaker position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members, I know, criticised MOF's fiscal marksmanship.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look, when I started work in MOF decades ago, one of my main tasks was to provide fiscal projections, as an economist.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I was one of those who would run the models and churn out the figures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I know exactly what this work entails and how difficult it is.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will not defend the figures if they are off the mark.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I will speak up for our MOF officers who do this work with dedication and professionalism against any unfair criticisms.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is based on the best available information at that point in time.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to make assumptions and we have to decide how we deal with uncertainties.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a crisis, when there is greater volatility in the economy, it is inherently more difficult to predict the turning points.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if you set aside unexpected crises like COVID-19, our operating revenue projections have generally not been far off the mark.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The average deviation over the 10-year period from FY2010 to FY2019 was within a reasonable range of 5%.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us dive deeper into the FY2024 projections because there were some questions raised about that.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Louis Chua had filed a written Parliamentary Question in September asking about the overall fiscal position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our reply referred to the figure reported in the Budget Book, which was also the figure provided in the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, MOF only starts to put together the revised fiscal estimates around the December and January period, when we start to get more data to update our estimates.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as I have explained in the Budget Statement, one key reason for the revenue upside was the unexpected increase in corporate income tax collections.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another reason, more generally, is that our economy performed better than expected, the Singapore economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also the forecasts of many, in fact, I would say, virtually all private sector professional economists.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, when you have higher growth, it means higher incomes, which drives consumption and that shows up in higher collections – for GST, for example, and the Certificates of Entitlement (COEs).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim suggested that the COE collections were driven by Government policy which kept prices high.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, in fact, it was the opposite effect.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it also meant more motor vehicle sales; and then, with more sales and more quantity purchased, that is why you have more revenues.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is not a price effect, it is a quantity effect.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In most other countries, poor budget marksmanship is when a government severely overestimates the revenue it will collect and underestimates its expenditure.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, the government makes unfunded promises that it cannot see through because there is no money or it borrows funds from somewhere else and kicks the can down the road, and leaves behind a growing burden for the next generation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this is not the case in Singapore, where we practise responsible and prudent budgeting.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, it is not just the matter of good marksmanship or poor marksmanship.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a question of the right values and the wrong values, the correct fiscal principles and the wrong principles.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the WP and PSP may think we are being overly cautious in our projections.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this Government will never take risks with Singaporeans' lives and future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We keep our public finances healthy year after year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if there are new or additional areas of need, we raise revenues to meet these new demands.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We always ensure that we have enough, rather than risk falling behind and falling short.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And should we have surpluses, that is good news.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The money is not squandered, because it helps to fund future needs and allows us to provide more support for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the fruits of Singapore's progress will be shared with everyone – as we are doing in Budget, to recognise the collective efforts of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have 60 years of history to show that Singapore has abided by the right values and principles and Singaporeans can continue to count on this Government to continue doing the same.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are in a fortunate position to have surpluses in FY2024 and FY2025.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But on the expenditure side, I fully expect our spending to increase in the coming years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai commented that the monies are going into more and more endowment and trust funds.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, in fact, the majority of these funds are drawdown funds.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, the monies within these funds are going to be withdrawn and spent for upcoming needs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The monies that we set aside will be spent very soon, as construction on Terminal 5 (T5) begins this year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Changi Airport is owned by the Changi Airport Group (CAG).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not owned directly by the Government.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the T5 project is not eligible for SINGA borrowing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, CAG will borrow for the project and the Government will be providing a guarantee to help lower borrowing costs, as I explained in my Budget Statement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if we want Changi Airport to remain competitive as a global air hub, CAG cannot rely on borrowing alone to cover the full costs of the project and that is why the Government is providing significant support and funding through grants.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will continue to be responsible and prudent with our finances.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if we maintain this approach, our reserves should be able to keep pace with our economy and we can continue to benefit from a steady stream of Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) in our revenue stream.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Compare this with the fiscal situation in so many other advanced economies around the world, especially in the West.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are running record levels of fiscal deficits, and their national debts are growing faster than their economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the fiscal space they have to sustain their higher levels of welfare, while continuing to invest in defence and the economy, is shrinking.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And at some point, the reckoning will come.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You do not even have to go far afield to look at western countries.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look nearer to home at what is happening in Hong Kong, which several Members also talked about.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It used to have a healthy fiscal position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But look how quickly the situation can turn and how they are grappling with deficits now and have to take such drastic steps to consolidate their position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, really, we should appreciate all that we have here in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In contrast to so many other countries which are using their revenues to service interest payments, we have the opposite.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We receive a boost to our revenues from our investment returns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Countries that have this luxury of investment returns are the ones that are endowed with oil and gas, or some other natural resource.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have been blessed by the heavens with these endowments.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have nothing, and yet, we are in this position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is truly unique, and it is a Singapore miracle.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our fiscal strength is a vital source of competitive advantage in these turbulent times.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: No one can predict what the next few years will bring.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have already seen wars in Europe and the Middle East.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to be prepared for a whole spectrum of possible global disruptions and threats.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And in today's environment, sadly, global responses to these threats may not be as well-coordinated and effective as before.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in Singapore, we know that if such shocks were to arise, we have the ability to respond swiftly to them, like we did during COVID-19.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will continue to focus on accountability in spending, to ensure value for money in everything we spend.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are existing mechanisms in place to scrutinise our spending plans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will not go through all of them, but we have well-established mechanisms to do so.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government continues to put out regular reporting of outcomes in the Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Review as well as KPIs in the Budget Book.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as Mr Pritam Singh himself noted, we have put out occasional papers wherever relevant, for example, MOF's occasional paper on our COVID-19 measures, our occasional paper on medium-term projections, which I said we will be updating, as well as MTI's report card on the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will continue to do so wherever useful.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the whole, we have achieved outcomes that reflect our values as a society, one that is fair and equitable, prudent yet progressive, where those who have more contribute more to uplift those with less.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we did extend some measures to private property residents, arising from feedback from the residents themselves as well as from many Members.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Pritam Singh says it is "ironic" that they should receive climate vouchers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is an effort to encourage everyone to do their part to be more energy-efficient.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But more importantly, let us look at the overall picture.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We continue to have a highly progressive tax and transfer system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members are familiar with the benefits and tax ratios which we highlight every Budget, and it is worth going through them again.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Middle-income households also get more benefits than tax paid, as we go through the income thresholds and levels.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is what our system has achieved, and these outcomes are a culmination of years of deliberate moves to enhance the progressivity of our overall taxes and transfers system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no fiscal system in the world that can deliver perfect precision and equity.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
